newsitem.title: FRANCE: French hotel group Accor profits rise.
newsitem.headline: French hotel group Accor profits rise.

text.p: French hotel group Accor reported on Wednesday its 1996 profit rose 14.6 percent to 1.06 billion francs ($183 million), helped by gains from the sale and leaseback of hotels.
However, Accor's operating profit fell to 2.58 billion francs from 2.92 billion, reflecting weakness in the leisure industry in Europe, notably in the first half of 1996.
Accor management board chairman Jean-Marc Espalioux told a news conference business remains sluggish in Germany but the year was off to a good start in the other regions.

The company sharply reduced its financial expenses to 1.26 billion francs from 1.46 billion after reducing debt to 17.5 billion francs at the end of 1996 from 19.4 billion at the end of the preceding year, bringing debt levels below equity.

Accor's bottom-line results were also helped by an improved performance at Europcar, its 50-50 car rental venture with Volkswagen. Europcar's loss shrank to 19 million francs last year from a loss of 152 million in 1995.

Sales at Accor, whose hotels range from the upscale Sofitel chain to downscale U.S.-based Motel 6, totalled 28.31 billion francs last year. Although the result was below 1995 sales of 31 billion, turnover on a like-for-like basis rose 2.9 percent.

Accor said it would buy out minority stakeholders in the economy hotel segment, which groups the Ibis, ETAP and Formule 1 chains. Accor, which holds 77 percent of the unit called Sphere International, will offer one Accor share for seven in Sphere.

"From 1997, given the parity of seven Sphere International shares for one in Accor leading to the creation of 2,347,761 Accor shares, this transaction will have a beneficial impact of more than two francs per share," it said in a statement.

The one-star hotel business is expanding at a brisk pace. Accor expects the business to show a 300 million franc profit, excluding exceptionals, in 1997, up 25 percent. The economy segment accounts for roughly a quarter of Accor sales.

Paribas Capital Markets said in a research note that the buyout of Sphere was "excellent news for Accor, as it is buying at near the bottom of the cycle and into a business which has long-term growth prospects on a global basis". Paribas reinforced its 'buy' recommendation on the stock.
Accor's Espalioux declined to give a group forecast.
Officials said Europcar was expected to show a profit next year of 50 million francs and the objective was to reach around 200 million in three years.
Accor's profit was slightly higher than the market consensus forecast of 1.05 billion francs. ($ = 5.781 French Francs)
